newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Gaelic Games-Meath claim sixth All-Ireland title.
newsitem.headline: Gaelic Games-Meath claim sixth All-Ireland title.

text.p: A last-minute point from forward Brendan Reilly earned Meath their sixth All-Ireland football title on Sunday and dashed Mayo's hopes of winning the Sam Maguire trophy for the first time in 45 years.

With just seconds remaining, Reilly put the ball over the bar to score his first point of the match and secure a 2-9 (15) to 1-11 (14) victory over Mayo in a windswept 1996 All-Ireland final replay at Croke Park.
"It was an unbelievable game. The conditions were terrible because everybody hates the wind. But it was an unbelievable fight back," Meath manager Sean Boylan said after the match.

Mayo, who played with the wind in the first half, were ahead for most of a highly-charged game until a 60th minute goal from Meath captain Tommy Dowd turned the tables and put the Leinster champions one point up.

As the minutes ticked away, Mayo's James Horan equalised but a thrilling finish saw Reilly clinch the match for Meath. Drifting out to the right hand side, Reilly picked up the ball and moved around his marker to make a better angle for himself before coolly popping over the winning score.
The Connacht champions had taken control in the first half with the aid of the strong wind, although a brawl in the early minutes of the game reduced both sides to just 14 men.

A fifth-minute free kick by Maurice Sheridan dropped in front of the Meath goal and in the tussle for possession, tempers frayed and punches were thrown in a fracas involving most of the players on the field.
Mayo mid-fielder Liam McHale and Meath defender Colm Coyle paid the price for the general outburst as referee Pat McEnaney sent both players off.
But Mayo soon settled to the task at hand and Horan went on to score the first point of the match in the 11th minute.
The Connacht men then notched up three more points before Meath's Trevor Giles countered with a point taken from a free in the 20th minute.
Both sides secured another point each before a long ball from Mayo captain Noel Connelly saw substitute P.J. Loftus score the first goal of the match in the 33rd minute.
Loftus, who had earlier replaced forward Ray Dempsey, pounced on a break from Anthony Finnerty to slot the ball into the back of the net.
But Meath quickly fought back and a foul on Tommy Dowd earned them a penalty.
Trevor Giles, the 21-year old student who scored nearly half of Meath's total tally, made no mistakes, tucking the ball into the corner of the net with clinical precision.
A point from Maurice Sheridan in injury time left Mayo four points ahead at the half-time whistle on a scoreline of 1-6 (9) to 1-2 (5).
With the wind behind them, Meath came roaring back to score three points in the opening minutes of the second half, leaving a one-point gap between the sides.
Despite a strong breeze, Mayo hung on to their narrow lead with grim determination as the sides traded points.
But Dowd's goal, scored from a quickly-taken free, proved decisive, ending Mayo's dreams of glory and earning Meath their first football title since 1988.

MAYO, 1-John Madden; 2-Kenneth Mortimer, 3-Kevin Cahill, 4-Dermot Flanagan (replaced by Pat Fallon in the 45th minute); 5-Pat Holmes, 6-James Nallen, 7-Noel Connelly (Captain); 8-Liam McHale, 9-David Brady; 10-James Horan (0-5), 11-Colm McManamon, 12-Maurice Sheridan (0-5); 13-Anthony Finnerty, 14-John Casey (0-1), 15-Ray Dempsey (replaced by P.J. Loftus (1-0) in the 26th minute).

MEATH, 1-Conor Martin, 2-Mark O'Reilly, 3-Darren Fay, 4-Martin O'Connell; 5-Colm Coyle, 6-Enda McManus, 7-Paddy Reynolds; 8-Jimmy McGuinness, 9-John McDermott; 10-Trevor Giles (1-4), 11-Tommy Dowd (Captain 1-3), 12-Graham Geraghty; 13-Colm Brady, 14-Brendan Reilly (0-1), 15-Barry Callaghan (0-1, replaced by Jody Devine in the 66th minute).
